Analysis: Hypothesis 2 is favored because it focuses on a more concrete and modular intervention—upregulating PGC-1α to drive changes in mitochondrial biogenesis and SER remodeling—that lends itself to a well-defined and testable experimental design. Although both hypotheses are novel, Hypothesis 1’s attempt to link CTNNB1 mutation‐driven Wnt/β‑catenin activation with broad metabolic reprogramming and chemoresistance raises concerns about mechanistic oversimplification and model-specific limitations. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 benefits from clearly demarcating its experimental variables (CRISPR activation, epigenetic modulation, and cell density optimization) that can be investigated in a phased manner. This improves its plausibility and testability. Both approaches are in vitro and pose minimal safety concerns; however, the comprehensive, clearer framework in Hypothesis 2 makes it the better overall idea.
